newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola closes lower on weak CBOT soy, hedges.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola closes lower on weak CBOT soy, hedges.

text.p: WCE canola closed easier and near the day's lows due to late hedge-related selling and weakness in CBOT soybeans.

Dealers also noted the leading crusher who had been a major buyer of March and November recently appeared to be largely absent from the futures market Wednesday, removing one of this week's main supportive influences.

The continued weakness of the yen versus the Canadian dollar remained a background depressive factor with Japanese interest in canola imports currently limited to a few "hand-to-mouth" purchases. March canola ended $5.00 lower at $402.70.
Flaxseed also closed lower weakened by hedge selling.
"Late hedges didn't find too much support," a dealer said.
Western barley closed higher, aided mainly by the strength of the February contract where commercials covered shorts.
"The shorts are getting out of the February and that is keeping a floor under the market," one dealer said.
Wheat prices were lower with locals offering it down late amid sentiment the market remains overvalued.
The slow pace of farmer selling, however, continued to underpin the market.
March feed wheat was down $1.00 at $168.00.
May feed peas closed up US$0.50 at US$196.00 while oats remained tradeless.
(All values in Canadian dollars/tonne except peas, oats)
